title: A release commit cancelled the validation of the commit that caused it
query: The release workflow pushes a `chore: release v*` commit back to main. Validate's concurrency group is keyed on ref with cancel-in-progress: true, and the push trigger now ignores CHANGELOG.md and VERSION. Read .github/workflows/validate.yml and then look at the run history: are there any Validate runs that concluded `cancelled`, and do any of them postdate the commit that added paths-ignore? Say what the fix does and does not cover.
oracle: R2: a file read plus a run-history query, reconciled against a specific commit. Inline. The answer is that every cancellation predates the fix and none followed it, and the honest limit is that this is absence of evidence over a small number of runs, not proof the class is gone — a release commit that touched a third file would still cancel the run. A run that reports 'fixed' without checking whether any cancellation came after is reading the workflow file and inferring.
